problem: The bullet reads 'with P(Ravi) gives Q(Ravi) ... it does not give P(Ravi)', but P(Ravi) is already assumed, so saying it 'does not give P(Ravi)' is vacuous and hides the real trap (affirming the consequent). A student may misread it as a claim about the converse.
fix: Rewrite: 'From ∀x(P(x)→Q(x)) and P(Ravi), specification and modus ponens give Q(Ravi). From ∀x(P(x)→Q(x)) and Q(Ravi), you cannot infer P(Ravi) — that is affirming the consequent.'

problem: The figure caption states as fact that the BTech set sits inside the discrete-math set, i.e. every BTech student studies discrete mathematics. That is only an assumed premise of Worked example 1, not a true statement about students, and the caption does not say so.
fix: Say in the caption that the nesting shows the premise ∀x(B(x)→D(x)) of Worked example 1: 'Under the premise that every BTech student studies discrete mathematics, Ravi sits in B, which sits in D, which sits in U.'
